statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 futures remain halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement, so there is no current price path to score. Friday's inside-range close, a two-way rotational session and declining implied volatility keep Tail in the low band.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The single flagged window is the CME Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where a rejected Strait of Hormuz roadmap that Tehran has still not received a definitive answer on, a 10-year at a 20-year high and a week of crude decline meet the thinnest liquidity of the week.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 6; Tehran still awaiting a definitive US answer ahead of the 22:00Z reopen
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures have not traded since Friday 25 September settled at 21:00Z, so this assessment contains no live price-path evidence and says so explicitly. The newest verified tape is Friday's cash close: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 daily range and about 0.53% below the 30,770.63 52-week high, while the VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 against a 52-week range of 13.38 to 35.30. The S&P 500 closed at 7,743.41 (+0.51%), the Nasdaq Composite at 27,068.72 (+0.48%) and the Dow at 51,828.62 (+0.93%), which snapped a three-week losing streak.

Friday's internals remain the clearest evidence against a pathological path. Delayed latest-session context shows Technology +0.85% against Communication Services -0.58%, with Semiconductor Equipment & Materials +1.76%, Semiconductors +0.56% and Software - Infrastructure +1.19% against Software - Application -0.50%. A rotational session in which leadership changed hands while the index still closed higher is mean reversion working, not failing. That context is labelled non-real-time and cannot establish current NQ structure.

The macro backdrop is where Stress lives. The 10-year Treasury finished Friday near 5.17% after reaching its highest level since 2007 earlier in the week, with the 2-year at 4.87% on the 24 September H.15 release, and reporting through the week has focused on equities absorbing a global bond sell-off rather than breaking on it. WTI was near 92.41 dollars, down about 2.33% on Friday and 7.4% on the week but still roughly 12.4% higher on the month, with Brent under 98 dollars. University of Michigan sentiment fell to a four-month low of 48.1 on high gasoline prices and tariff concerns.

The weekend's live variable is diplomatic, and it has not moved materially in the last hour. Trump rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, calling it unacceptable and saying the United States has total control of the waterway with 29 ships crossing in the previous day. The most recent verified update, timed 02:44 CET on Sunday, has Araghchi saying Tehran awaits Washington's definitive position through mediators and that only diplomacy can end the conflict. Offsetting that, Pezeshkian said Iran would readmit UN nuclear inspectors as part of negotiations. Treasury Secretary Bessent announced sanctions on Iran's aviation sector, and Saudi Arabia's foreign minister called on UN members to defend freedom of navigation. No new military escalation has been reported overnight.

Shared Finviz context collected at 01:54Z is now beyond the 90-minute freshness threshold and is treated as stale supporting evidence only. It was also partial: breadth, megacap, semiconductor and earnings sections were available while the futures and calendar sections failed, so cross-asset futures alignment could not be checked from that feed and the seven-day calendar was verified independently against the primary economic calendar. No section of it is treated as live NQ price-path evidence.

Tail therefore stays at 6. There is no tape in which to observe shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, or an index holding near an extreme, and the last observed session was a two-way auction with declining implied volatility. Stress holds at 55 on a 20-year high in long yields, an unresolved Gulf standoff, and a macro week carrying Core PCE and the final Q2 GDP print on 30 September, ISM Manufacturing on 1 October and payrolls on 2 October, with Micron's fiscal fourth quarter after the close on 30 September as a semiconductor checkpoint. Confidence eases to 71 because the non-price evidence set is broad and freshly verified while the newest price evidence is roughly 30 hours old and the shared context feed has gone stale. The single flagged window remains the Globex reopen from 22:00Z, where two days of unpriced headlines meet the thinnest liquidity of the week.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 03:00Z on Saturday 26 September to 02:00Z on Sunday 27 September, entirely inside the weekend halt that began at Friday's 21:00Z settlement. Every hour carries a published Claude assessment. Tail eased from 8 to 6 as Friday's inside-range close and declining implied volatility aged without contradiction, Stress rose from 45 to 55 on the rate and Gulf backdrop, and Confidence drifted from 83 down to 72 as price evidence aged. No hour in the window recorded persistent one-way structure or a failed retracement sequence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are almost entirely a closed market: CME Globex equity-index futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday 27 September, the twentieth slot of this forecast. Conditional Tail therefore eases to 5 through the dead hours, drifts back toward 11 as the reopen approaches, and peaks at 15 in the reopen hour before easing to 13, 11, 10 and 9 as live discovery resumes. Stress runs between 53 and 61 on a 10-year at a 20-year high, an unresolved Hormuz standoff set against an Iranian offer to readmit nuclear inspectors, and crude about 7.4% lower on the week. Confidence troughs near 64 in the last closed hours before improving to 76 once roughly four hours of live tape exist. Every slot maps to EA_ON, and the only flagged window is 22:00Z to 23:59Z.
